title: Pesto-Stuffed Portobello Burgers
changes_from_base: No patty: whole portobello caps, gills scooped out, are marinated with olive oil, garlic and basil, pan-cooked until juicy, then filled with pesto and warmed through; buns optional.
summary: Meaty portobello caps caramelise in olive oil until golden, then are filled with fragrant basil pesto and cooked until tender, juicy and warm right through.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Using a teaspoon, pull out the stalks from 4 large portobello mushrooms, then scrape out and discard the gills to create a cavity for the filling.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Toss the mushroom caps in a large bowl with 2 tbsp of the extra-virgin olive oil, ½ tsp fine salt, ¼ tsp ground black pepper, 1 crushed garlic clove and 2 tbsp finely chopped basil. Leave to marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Cook first side
steps.text: Heat the remaining 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil in a large heavy frying pan over a medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the marinated mushroom caps rounded side down, working in batches if needed, and cook without moving them for 7 minutes until golden brown underneath.

steps.title: Cook second side
steps.text: Turn the caps over and continue cooking for 5-7 minutes as they slowly release their liquid onto the pan.

steps.title: Stuff and finish
steps.text: Turn the caps over cavity side up, spread a heaped teaspoon of basil pesto into each one, then cook for a further 2 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and juicy and any liquid pooled in the pan has evaporated.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer the hot stuffed mushrooms to split burger buns if you like, or serve them as they are on the plate.

tips: Shop pesto contains Parmesan and usually pine nuts, and some brands use cashews, so check the label.
Cook them rounded side down first to caramelise the surface and develop a savoury depth of flavour before you flip them.
If the liquid hasn't fully evaporated by the time the pesto is hot, let it cook uncovered for another minute to dry out and concentrate the flavours.
storage: Best served warm, straight from the pan, either as a stand-alone dish or tucked into a burger bun. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
